cases.sentence: Ich glaube, dass der junge Arzt den Bericht lesen wird.

relations.relation: internal theta-role and accusative Case assignment

derivationStages.stageRecord: The analysis uses classical NP structure, head-final German VP and IP structure, and head-initial CP structure. Determiners occupy Spec-NP; junge is an AP adjunct to N′ inside the embedded subject. The object den Bericht is the complement of lesen. A higher verbal projection contains the future auxiliary wird, which selects the infinitival VP den Bericht lesen. Wird is therefore an auxiliary, not a copular or lexical predicate. Ich, the complementizer dass, and the matrix verb glaube remain separate objects pending clause construction. Inflected words are represented as whole lexical terminals; no separate morphological realization is needed. Subjects will be base-generated in Spec-IP, with their external theta roles supplied by their predicates, rather than introduced inside VP.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the nominal phrases and the embedded head-final verbal structure.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The auxiliary VP combines with a right-headed finite I, and der junge Arzt occupies Spec-IP. In this classical subject-placement analysis, lesen supplies the subject's external agent theta role through the verbal predicate; the future auxiliary introduces no additional participant theta role. Finite I licenses nominative Case and third-person singular agreement. The auxiliary remains in its previously established V position, so this workspace explicitly supplies the source for its subsequent movement to I.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the embedded IP with its subject and finite inflection.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Wird moves from the auxiliary V position shown in the preceding workspace to the immediately higher finite I. Its lower position becomes an unpronounced head trace, and the pronounced auxiliary is incorporated into I. Because I is right-headed, this movement preserves the surface sequence den Bericht lesen wird. Present-tense inflection belongs to the auxiliary, while the construction receives its future interpretation from the auxiliary's selection of the infinitival VP.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the embedded finite auxiliary from V to I.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Dass combines with the completed IP as the overt, initial C of a declarative complement clause. Spec-CP is unfilled and therefore is not represented by an empty placeholder. The occupied C position does not attract the finite auxiliary: wird remains in final I, distinguishing this embedded clause from the matrix V2 clause. The embedded CP is now available as the propositional complement of glaube.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the dass-clause as an embedded CP.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Glaube selects the embedded CP as its propositional complement. Under the uniformly head-final VP analysis adopted here, that complement is initially to the left of the matrix V. The resulting VP combines with right-headed finite I, and Ich is base-generated in Spec-IP. Glaube assigns its external experiencer theta role to Ich and its propositional theta role to the CP; matrix finite I licenses nominative Case and first-person singular agreement. This is a pre-extraposition, pre-V2 workspace, not the surface order.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the matrix D-structure with the CP in its selected complement position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The embedded CP moves from the matrix verb's complement position to a right-adjoined position on VP. Its source is the complement position explicitly shown in the preceding stage, and a silent CP trace now occupies that position. The extraposition chain preserves the CP's selected-complement status and propositional theta role: right adjunction here does not turn the dass-clause into an independently interpreted adjunct. This movement supplies the sentence's postverbal complement placement within the adopted head-final analysis.
derivationStages.statement: Extrapose the selected complement CP to the right edge of the matrix VP.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Glaube moves from its matrix V position to finite I, leaving an unpronounced V trace. The extraposed CP and all of its internal structure remain unchanged. This intermediate workspace is required because the next head movement starts from I rather than moving directly from V to C. The already inflected lexical word glaube is pronounced at I at this stage; no additional morphological pieces are introduced.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the matrix finite verb from V to I.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A matrix CP is projected above IP. The finite I containing glaube moves from the I position established in the preceding stage into C, leaving an I trace. Ich then moves from Spec-IP to Spec-CP, leaving an NP trace. The first dependency implements German root-clause V2; the second fills the preverbal field with the subject. Ich retains the nominative Case and experiencer theta role licensed at its lower position, and its fronting is an A-bar dependency rather than new theta-role assignment. The embedded clause remains introduced by dass with final wird, and the CP extraposition chain remains intact. Reading only pronounced terminals yields exactly Ich glaube dass der junge Arzt den Bericht lesen wird. No binding ambiguity or competing attachment is supported by this sentence; temporal versus modal nuances of the future auxiliary do not require distinct syntactic structures.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix V2 clause by I-to-C movement and subject fronting.

cases.sentence: No student has ever read this book.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The negative quantificational determiner “No” combines with the nominal projection headed by “student,” yielding the subject DP. The demonstrative “this” combines with the nominal projection headed by “book,” yielding the object DP. “Ever” is projected as an adverbial phrase. “Read” is selected in its participial form because it will be the complement of perfect “has”; the spelling is syncretic with other forms of the verb, so no additional morphological decomposition is required.
derivationStages.statement: The two determiner phrases and the lexical predicate material are projected.

relations.relation: Structural objective Case assignment under government

derivationStages.stageRecord: The transitive participle “read” first merges with the object DP “this book,” assigning it the Theme role. AdvP “ever” is then left-adjoined to V′, placing it before the verb without intervening between the verb and its selected object. The subject DP “No student” is merged in Spec-VP and receives the Agent role. This VP-internal subject position is the source position required for the later A-movement analysis. The verb governs and assigns structural objective Case to its DP complement. Polarity licensing is not yet evaluated as a surface or LF condition.
derivationStages.statement: The lexical VP is formed with the object as complement, “ever” as a V′ adjunct, and the subject in the external theta position.

relations.relation: Structural objective Case assignment under government
A-movement to the finite subject position
Theta-role preservation in the subject A-chain

values.licensingConfiguration: The negative subject DP c-commands ever in its VP scope.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Finite present-perfect “has” is generated in I and selects the participial VP; this analysis therefore does not derive “has” by head movement from V. IP is projected above I′. The subject DP moves from Spec-VP to Spec-IP, leaving a silent DP trace with the same lineage. The raised DP satisfies the Extended Projection Principle and receives nominative Case from finite I. Its singular nominal head controls third-person singular agreement, yielding “has.” The Agent theta role remains associated with the lower position and is borne by the entire A-chain, so movement does not create a second theta role. In Spec-IP the negative DP c-commands the V′-adjunct “ever”; its negative quantificational force therefore licenses the polarity item. No movement of either “No” or “ever” is needed for this scope relation.
derivationStages.statement: Finite perfect I is merged and the subject undergoes A-movement from Spec-VP to Spec-IP.

relations.relation: Structural objective Case assignment under government
Theta-role preservation in the subject A-chain

values.licensingConfiguration: The negative subject DP c-commands ever.

values.scopeOrder: no student > ever > read this book

derivationStages.stageRecord: A phonologically null declarative C selects the finite IP and projects CP. Because this is a declarative clause, neither subject–auxiliary inversion nor movement to Spec-CP occurs. The completed representation has one theta-marked subject A-chain, a Theme object, nominative Case on the raised subject, objective Case on the object, and finite subject–I agreement. The negative quantificational DP in Spec-IP takes scope over the VP and licenses “ever” by c-command. The V′ attachment of “ever” places its temporal existential contribution inside the perfect predicate, giving the reading that there is no student for whom a reading of this book has occurred at any relevant time. The null C contributes declarative force. No Case Filter, Theta Criterion, EPP, binding-theoretic, government, or polarity-licensing violation arises, so the exact input is grammatical in this analysis.
derivationStages.statement: A null declarative C completes the CP, and the resulting representation satisfies the relevant GB conditions.

relations.relation: Lexical inflection and passive argument structure

values.externalArgument: not projected as a grammatical subject

derivationStages.stageRecord: The ordinary reading is ‘These books have been read by children.’ A lexicalist GB analysis selects vimesomwa as an already inflected passive verb: vi- expresses class-8 subject agreement, -me- perfect aspect, -som- the reading predicate, -w- passive morphology, and -a the final vowel. These are properties of one lexical terminal, not separately generated syntactic heads. The passive lacks structural accusative Case and does not project its external argument as a subject. Vitabu hivi forms a DP with a silent determiner and a demonstrative right-adjoined to N′; this preserves the noun–demonstrative order without moving the noun. Vitabu and hivi exhibit class-8 concord. Watoto forms a class-2 plural DP. Na heads a PP and licenses the children's DP with oblique Case. On this reading, that PP will identify the passive predicate's external participant. Abstract finite I carries perfect and class-8 agreement features, whose subject licensing is not yet established.
derivationStages.statement: Select the passive verb and construct the nominal expressions and agentive prepositional phrase.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The passive verb first takes the books DP as its complement, establishing the Theme position. The agent PP is then right-adjoined to V′ within VP. Its nominal identifies the reading event's external participant, but neither the PP nor its nominal occupies the grammatical subject position. I combines with this VP to form I′ and an IP whose subject specifier is not yet filled. The books remain in the verb's complement position: they receive the Theme role there but cannot receive structural accusative from this passive verb. This unsatisfied Case requirement motivates the subsequent passive A-movement.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the underlying passive clause with the books in object position.

relations.relation: Government of the passive object trace

values.dependency: governed lower member of the passive A-chain

derivationStages.stageRecord: The books DP moves from the previously established complement of V to Spec-IP, leaving a silent DP trace rather than an unpronounced full copy. The resulting A-chain receives its single Theme role through the lower position and nominative Case through the upper position. Finite I licenses nominative, its subject requirement is satisfied, and its class-8 agreement is checked against Vitabu hivi. The agent DP remains inside the PP, with its independently licensed oblique Case. This derives a passive subject without assigning that subject an Agent role.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the books DP to the finite subject position.

values.morphologicalCommitment: lexically inflected verb; no syntactic affix fusion

relations.relation: Government through the verbal head chain

values.dependency: government preserved through the V-to-I chain

derivationStages.stageRecord: The inflected verb raises from its established V position and adjoins to I, leaving a silent head trace. This analysis adopts overt V-to-I movement for the Swahili finite verb; movement positions the already inflected lexical word and does not manufacture its morphological spelling. The resulting complex I head contains the pronounced verb and an unpronounced inflectional feature head. The lower V trace remains connected to the moved lexical governor, preserving the government dependency of the passive object trace. A silent declarative C projects CP over the completed IP. The pronounced yield is exactly Vitabu hivi vimesomwa na watoto, with watoto interpreted as the readers.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the finite declarative clause by V-to-I movement.
